steps.description: Fit the paired model on the raw counts. Pre-filter minimally: keep a gene only if it reaches at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples (the smallest group size). Build a DESeqDataSet with colData holding subject (4 levels) and condition, set the condition reference level explicitly to control with relevel, and use design ~ subject + condition so the subject term absorbs between-subject variation. Normalization is median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside DESeq2 — do not pre-scale the counts. Run the likelihood ratio test with full = ~subject + condition and reduced = ~subject; this is the answer to 'responds to either treatment'. Then re-fit or extract Wald statistics for three named contrasts, each written as (condition, numerator, denominator): (condition, treated_a, control), (condition, treated_b, control), and (condition, treated_b, treated_a). Shrink log fold changes with ashr for every contrast — apeglm cannot take the treated_b vs treated_a contrast because it is not a single model coefficient, so use one estimator across all three for comparability. Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha=0.05 within each contrast and within the LRT separately, with independent filtering on and alpha passed to results() matching the reporting cutoff. Before trusting the adjusted values, plot the raw p-value histogram for the LRT and for each contrast and describe its shape. Emit one results table per contrast plus the LRT table, each carrying gene symbol, baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken log2FoldChange (ashr), stat, pvalue, padj, and a column naming the contrast. plan.title: Paired 3-condition DE: treated_a/treated_b vs control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000 x 12 raw Salmon gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12-row sample table (metadata.csv: subject, condition). Four subjects each contribute one control, one treated_a and one treated_b sample — a complete within-subject block over three conditions, single batch, n=4 per condition. The research question has two parts: (1) which genes respond to either treatment within a subject, and (2) whether the two treatments differ from each other. Both parts are answered by one blocked negative-binomial model with subject as a fixed blocking term: design ~ subject + condition. Part (1) is the DESeq2 likelihood ratio test of ~subject+condition against ~subject — an omnibus test for any condition effect within subject — plus the two Wald contrasts treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control. Part (2) is the third Wald contrast treated_b vs treated_a, which is a contrast between two non-reference levels rather than a model coefficient, so it must be named as (condition, treated_b, treated_a) and its log fold changes shrunk with ashr rather than apeglm.

Step order: T1S1 profiles sample structure on a blind VST (PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) and specifically checks whether samples pair by subject — with 4 subjects and 12 samples, a subject effect that dominates PC1 is expected and is exactly why the block belongs in the design. T1S2 fits the model, runs the LRT and the three Wald contrasts, applies ashr shrinkage, and adjusts p-values with BH within each contrast. T1S3 is an independent second-method check with edgeR quasi-likelihood on the same design, because at n=4 per group DESeq2 and edgeR agree on most genes but not all; the intersection is reported as the high-confidence set. T2S1 runs preranked fgsea per contrast on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against human Hallmark, Reactome and WikiPathways from the reference store — a ranked test rather than over-representation, since with 4 subjects the significant list may well be shorter than the ~50 genes an ORA needs. T1S4 assembles the report.

Power caveat stated up front: 4 subjects is small. The within-subject design is the main defence — it removes between-subject variance from every contrast — but the treated_b vs treated_a contrast is the least powered of the three, since it compares two perturbed states that may differ far less from each other than either does from control. A null result on that contrast is not evidence that the treatments are equivalent, and the report must say so rather than presenting it as a finding.

One data caveat: the profile says counts came from Salmon, but only a gene-level count matrix is provided — no transcript quantifications and no average transcript lengths. The recommended tximport length-offset path is therefore unavailable; the matrix is modelled as integer counts and the report must state that no length offset was carried, which leaves gene-level calls driven by isoform-usage shifts unaccounted for.

Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples (smallest group size)
Blocked design ~ subject + condition, control as reference level, named contrasts
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test (~subject+condition vs ~subject) then pairwise Wald contrasts
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, within contrast
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways, per contrast
Reproducible report with MA and dispersion plots, shrunken and unshrunken LFC, leading edge genes, sessionInfo
